scope: Operator-requested fractal RCA, source fixes and isolated recovery staging. Preserve original coordinator/cycle histories. Production cutover requires independently reviewed exact candidate and fresh runtime fencing.

snapshot.reference: Current source-bound development RCA; no production or historical evidence admission.

criticality.rationale: Recover failed integrity and ecology operation without data loss.

stpa.rationale: Unreviewed authority restoration could activate invalid leases or false evidence.

fmea.rationale: S4 O3 Det3 = RPN36 band4; history loss and false trust are major failures.

dependency.rationale: Verified coordinator and release dependencies are prerequisites of effectful automation.

impact.rationale: Repair affects coordination, provenance and supervised ecology availability.

ucas.constraint: Check safety class and inherited prerequisite urgency before score.

ucas.constraint: Authorization and effect constraints precede ranking.

decision.summary: User explicitly requested fractal RCA and fixes for all three observed failures. Execute scoped development repair and candidate construction while preserving production gates.
alternatives: Blind restart or remove max_manifest guard: rejected
Preserve evidence, identify causes, test a repair candidate and obtain independent review: selected
counterevidence: Main cockpit responds despite integrity failures
Existing stores enforce append-only triggers but do not necessarily validate each imported digest
assumptions: Development bootstrap remains necessary because the successor effect harness is not ready
User authorizes fixes and recovery preparation; review/fencing constraints remain
decision.forecast: A bounded RCA can distinguish valid recoverable bytes from untrusted history and eliminate mutable release binding in a tested candidate.
decision.falsifier: Any original history overwritten, tampered candidate accepted, or unchanged dependency failure bypassed.
acceptance: Fractal RCA contains symptom, hypothesis, evidence, constraint, owner, containment, falsifier and recovery
Regression tests reproduce each repairable producer/verification defect
Preserved-history candidate passes integrity and replay with explicit trust boundaries
Reviewed exact release candidate verifies dependencies and bounded startup before production recovery
decision.rollback: Keep canonical stores and existing releases intact; isolate all staging; revert only task-owned source hunks.
decision.reviewer: Independent candidate review required before recovery activation.
decision.budget: Existing pinned local tools; two BEAM schedulers; bounded database queries and isolated tests; no package downloads or paid calls.
residuals: Unrecoverable/foreign historical events cannot be made authentic by hashing
Canonical cutover depends on verified writer quiescence and runtime fencing
